A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynFocus work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after its references despite mentioning supplementary material; v2 includes Appendices A–E. The comparison assesses newly included documentation without assuming when the underlying experiments were performed.

before.justification: v1 reports original DynFocus benchmark results, component ablations, redundancy measurements and token-count comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional training-state, clustering, computational-cost, data-composition and hallucination analyses.

M1.justification: The DPE selection mechanism, CCE fine/coarse encoding and two-stage training framework remain. v2 elaborates the differentiable Top-K mechanism already described in v1; this establishes additional documentation rather than a replacement algorithm.

E1.justification: The quantitative benchmarks and training-data families remain, including VideoHallucer already represented in v1 Figure 2. Appendix E adds qualitative demonstrations of multi-turn video dialogue and imaginative story generation, modestly extending the demonstrated task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds Flash-Vstream comparisons for latency and matched training data, K-means and weighted K-means clustering comparisons, and additional VideoHallucer comparators including VideoLaVIT. These substantially expand the reported comparison framework beyond the retained main benchmark tables.

E3.justification: v1 Table 5 varies LV-Bench input counts across 16, 32, 100 and 200 frames; v2 Table 3 instead reports five prototype configurations at 200 frames. Added analyses introduce controlled training-data and freezing configurations, component-cost profiling, and prompted/unprompted hallucination comparisons. Newly disclosed default hyperparameters are separate documentation changes.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds training-state, computational-cost, clustering, training-data and long-video prototype sensitivity analyses, plus detailed hallucination diagnostics. Appendices D–E add spatial-prototype visualizations and conversational case studies. The existing compact-encoding ablation survives as Table 12, relocated from v1 Table 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests for model comparisons. Appendix A's newly disclosed 20-video redundancy sample concerns sampling for an existing descriptive analysis, rather than repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The LV-Bench result set is replaced: its best reported accuracy changes from 31.5 to 32.9 under different prototype/input configurations, so this is not a same-setting improvement. Numerous supplementary result entries are added for training, clustering, computational costs, data composition and hallucination categories. The main zero-shot QA, VCG-Bench, MLVU and VideoMME scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a selection-matrix formulation, linear optimization problem, perturbation-based expectation and Jacobian in Equations 5–7. v1 only asserted that linear programming enabled differentiable selection and deferred the details. This substantially expands the mathematical account of a central training mechanism.

C1.justification: The main claims remain memory-efficient dynamic video encoding through DPE and CCE, competitive short- and long-video understanding, and potential against hallucination. The revised contribution wording reiterates competitive/SOTA positioning already expressed in v1's figure caption and conclusion.

C2.justification: The appendices add explanations of training-state effects, extra-token computational overhead, and the dependence of prototype settings on video length. They also discuss possible CLEVRER domain mismatch, hallucination-related yes/no bias and differences in image-derived knowledge, substantially extending the interpretations and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C newly document redundancy estimation, frame sampling, clustering parameters, batch sizes, optimization, precision and training configuration. Appendix B supplies training times and module costs. v2 also specifies Vicuna-7B-1.5 and adds a code-repository link; these disclosures do not establish that the underlying retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting perturbed optimization, clustering alternatives and Flash-Vstream comparisons. Appendix B.3 explains more precisely how DynFocus relates to LLaMA-VID and Chat-UniVi, while the main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes clarify notation and terminology, expand the trainability explanation, relocate the compact-encoding discussion and benchmark descriptions into appendices, and add acknowledgments and an organized supplement.

P2.justification: v1's overview radar chart is removed, existing figures and tables are extensively repositioned, table highlighting changes, and the sensitivity panels are reordered to match their descriptions. v2 also adds numerous supplementary tables, conversational figures and a spatial-prototype visualization.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies implementation settings, matched-data controls, measured computational costs and detailed hallucination results that v1 only partially documents, improving transparency and support for the claims. However, the added Top-K derivation gives inconsistent dimensions for P, and Appendix C.1's pretraining learning rate of 2e-3 conflicts with Table 15's 1e-3. These unresolved inconsistencies temper the benefit of the expanded technical account.
